title: Microsoft 365: pay-as-you-go meter for SharePoint storage above the tenant quota
summary: The opt-in default, storage rate, rollout targets and warning that budgets do not stop billing are supported. Minor corrections should extend two shortened control paths, restore a category heading in the purchase path and acknowledge Microsoft's differing administrator-role lists.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a consumption-based meter for extra SharePoint storage.
claims.quote: Use the new PAYGO consumption-based meter to pay for your extra SharePoint storage needs.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The release phases are General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap General Availability target is January CY2027.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "June CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists only Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap says the meter integrates with Microsoft 365 Archive.
claims.quote: This reduces the operational overhead associated with purchasing extra storage packs and more seamlessly integrates with Microsoft 365 Archive.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The meter is admin-opt-in and off by default, so it does not start billing without administrator action.

claims.claim: Administrators enable pay-as-you-go SharePoint storage billing in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Admins can enable pay-as-you-go SharePoint storage billing in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Once enabled, storage above the included tenant quota is automatically billed by consumption without another approval.
claims.quote: Storage used above the included tenant quota will be automatically billed based on consumption.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Users; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft's notice says there is no impact to users.
claims.quote: There is no impact to users.

claims.claim: Office 365 Extra File Storage remains available as an alternative to consumption billing.
claims.quote: The existing Office 365 Extra File Storage add-on remains available if you prefer to manually increase your storage quota instead.

claims.claim: MC1330893 was updated on 9 November 2026.
claims.quote: Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the timeline.

claims.claim: Worldwide Public Preview rollout completed in June 2026.
claims.quote: Public Preview (Worldwide): We completed rollout in June 2026.

claims.claim: General Availability rollout is expected to begin in early January 2027.
claims.quote: General Availability (WW): We expect to begin rolling out in early January 2027 (previously early November)

claims.claim: General Availability rollout is expected to complete by late January 2027.
claims.quote: and to complete rolling by late January 2027 (previously end of November).

claims.claim: The previous General Availability start target was early November.
claims.quote: early January 2027 (previously early November)

claims.claim: The previous General Availability completion target was the end of November.
claims.quote: late January 2027 (previously end of November)

claims.claim: The supplied Microsoft notice sets no act-by date.
claims.quote: Act by: none; No immediate action is required.

claims.claim: The service to select is named Microsoft 365 SharePoint Storage.
claims.quote: When you reach "Step 4. Review and create the billing policy," select the Microsoft 365 SharePoint Storage service.

claims.claim: Consumption licensing and variable cost describe a meter counting GB of SharePoint data above the tenant quota.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 SharePoint Storage | The number of gigabytes (GB) of data that exceeds the SharePoint tenant quota. | $0.20/GB/month (shows on invoice as $0.00667/GB/day)

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; What's changing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Charges are billed through the Azure subscription linked during setup.
claims.quote: When you use pay-as-you-go services, you're billed using service meters in the Azure subscription that you specified when you set up pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Learn lists the SharePoint storage price as $0.20/GB/month.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 SharePoint Storage | The number of gigabytes (GB) of data that exceeds the SharePoint tenant quota. | $0.20/GB/month

claims.claim: The invoice shows $0.00667/GB/day.
claims.quote: $0.20/GB/month (shows on invoice as $0.00667/GB/day)

claims.claim: The Azure consumption discount applies to storage services.
claims.quote: The Azure consumption discount (ACD) applies to storage services.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Azure Consumption Commitment does not apply.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Azure Consumption Commitment (MACC) doesn't apply.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited pricing page does not distinguish preview pricing from General Availability pricing.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint pay-as-you-go storage billing policy quota pricing Microsoft 365 SharePoint Storage; opened syntex-pay-as-you-go-services in full; its SharePoint Storage row publishes one rate without a preview/GA distinction.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence; Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: The tenant needs at least one SharePoint licence or a licence that includes SharePoint.
claims.quote: The tenant must have at least one SharePoint license, or a license that includes SharePoint.

claims.claim: The billing setup prerequisites name roles, Azure rights and a SharePoint licence but no separate user licence for the meter.
claims.quote: The tenant must have at least one SharePoint license, or a license that includes SharePoint.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Roles
claims.claim: The billing article permits SharePoint Administrator, Billing Administrator, AI Administrator or Global Administrator for setup.
claims.quote: You must have one of the following roles to complete the tasks in this article: SharePoint Administrator; Billing Administrator; AI Administrator; Global Administrator
claims.fix: Retain the billing article's role list and add in Scope: "The storage-specific prerequisites page instead lists SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator; its SharePoint section refers to the shared OneDrive prerequisites: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/commerce/add-storage-space#prerequisites-for-adding-microsoft-365-onedrive-storage."

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Owner or Contributor rights on both the Azure subscription and resource group are required.
claims.quote: You must have Owner or Contributor rights to the Azure subscription and resource group.

claims.claim: The Azure subscription must be in the same tenant as Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: You must have an Azure subscription in the same tenant as Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: The resource group must be in that Azure subscription.
claims.quote: You must have an Azure resource group in that subscription.

claims.claim: An Azure subscription can be created during billing policy setup.
claims.quote: If you don't have an Azure subscription, you can create one during the billing policy setup process.

claims.claim: An Azure resource group can be created during billing policy setup.
claims.quote: If you don't have an Azure resource group, you can create one during the billing policy setup process.

claims.claim: Creating a new subscription in the admin center requires Billing Account Owner or Billing Account Contributor.
claims.quote: To create a new subscription in the Microsoft 365 admin center, you must be a Billing Account Owner or a Billing Account Contributor.

claims.claim: Learn says SharePoint Storage is in public preview for all commercial tenants as of June 2026.
claims.quote: As of June 2026, Microsoft 365 SharePoint storage is in public preview for all commercial tenants.

claims.claim: Education tenants are not currently supported.
claims.quote: This product isn't currently available to education, GCC, or Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet in China customers.

claims.claim: GCC customers are not currently supported.
claims.quote: This product isn't currently available to education, GCC, or Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet in China customers.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet in China customers are not currently supported.
claims.quote: This product isn't currently available to education, GCC, or Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet in China customers.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Enrolled tenants do not receive quota-related email notifications.
claims.quote: While your tenant is enrolled in Microsoft 365 SharePoint Storage, you don't receive quota-related email notifications and banner notifications in the SharePoint admin center

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Enrolled tenants do not receive quota-related SharePoint admin center banner notifications.
claims.quote: you don't receive quota-related email notifications and banner notifications in the SharePoint admin center because the tenant is considered within quota.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: An enrolled tenant is considered within quota.
claims.quote: because the tenant is considered within quota.

claims.claim: Multi-geo billing uses the tenant quota rather than each geo's quota.
claims.quote: If you have a multi-geo tenant that uses pay-as-you-go storage, billing is based on the tenant's storage quota, not each geo's quota.

claims.claim: Multi-geo billing starts when total storage usage across all geos exceeds the tenant quota.
claims.quote: Billing starts when the tenant's total storage usage across all geos exceeds the tenant quota.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[1]; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Region selected when creating the billing policy determines where tenant ID and usage data are stored.
claims.quote: From the Region drop-down list, select a region. This selection determines where the tenant ID and usage data are stored.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Disconnecting while over quota immediately resumes quota enforcement.
claims.quote: If you disconnect while your tenant is over its storage quota, enforcement of the quota resumes immediately.

claims.claim: Budgets are set at billing policy level, not for individual users, agents or sites.
claims.quote: You can only set budgets at the billing policy level, not for individual users, agents, or sites. This policy means any limits or alerts apply to all services and users under the policy.

claims.where: summary; controls[2].note; controls[3].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The budget only alerts: reaching 100% does not stop the service or billing.
claims.quote: Reaching 100% of your budget doesn't stop the service or billing.

claims.claim: Budget alert notifications can take up to 24 hours to reach recipients.
claims.quote: It can take up to 24 hours for recipients to receive budget alert notifications.

claims.claim: Consumption data can take up to four hours to appear in the spending graph.
claims.quote: Consumption data can take up to four hours to appear in the graph.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go usage and charges can be monitored in Microsoft Cost Management for Azure.
claims.quote: You can also monitor your pay-as-you-go usage and costs in Microsoft Cost Management for Azure.

claims.claim: The storage service billing policy covers all users.
claims.quote: Choosing users only applies to Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go services. For all other services, the All users option is automatically applied.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Alternative; Governance controls; controls[5].note
claims.claim: Office 365 Extra File Storage is a purchased add-on increasing allocated storage in 1-GB increments, not a switch for the new meter.
claims.quote: Use the Office 365 Extra File Storage add-on to add more storage in 1-GB increments. You can buy the add-on in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Subscriptions purchased through Volume Licensing or CSP cannot buy Office 365 Extra File Storage directly from Microsoft.
claims.quote: If you bought your subscription through Volume Licensing or a Cloud Solution Provider (CSP), you can't buy Office 365 Extra File Storage directly from Microsoft.

claims.claim: The Active sites storage figure excludes changes made within the last 24-48 hours.
claims.quote: The storage used doesn't include changes made within the last 24-48 hours.

claims.claim: The Graph report provides storage trends over a reporting period.
claims.quote: Get the trend of storage allocated and consumed during the reporting period.

claims.claim: The Graph storage usage report requires Reports.Read.All.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | Reports.Read.All | Not available. Application | Reports.Read.All | Not available.

claims.claim: The Graph report is a historical storage report rather than a live PAYGO billing balance.
claims.quote: Get the trend of storage allocated and consumed during the reporting period. The CSV file has the following headers for columns: Report Refresh Date; Site Type; Storage Used (Byte); Report Date; Report Period.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Services > Connect a policy > Connection status connects SharePoint Storage.
claims.quote: select the Services tab. For the service that you want to connect, in the Billing policy column, select Connect a policy. In the side panel, find the billing policy that you want to connect to, and then select the Connection status toggle to set it to Connected.

claims.claim: No PowerShell, Graph or REST call for connecting or disconnecting this SharePoint Storage service is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 SharePoint Storage connect disconnect billing policy Microsoft Graph beta PowerShell REST API; read add-storage-space, billing-node setup, Graph search results and New-SPOAppBillingPolicy; the latter governs an application, not this storage meter.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Disconnecting the service turns off this meter through the Connection status toggle.
claims.quote: Select the service that you want to disconnect. In the side panel, select the Billing policies tab. In the Connection status column, select the Connected toggle to turn it off.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Billing policies > Add a billing policy leads to Azure billing details.
claims.quote: go to Billing > Pay-as-you-go. On the Billing policies tab, select Add a billing policy. On the Billing details page, enter a name for the billing policy.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path to "Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Billing policies > Add a billing policy > Billing details". Retain the note explaining that the subscription, resource group and region are selected there, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/commerce/services/pay-as-you-go-setup-billing-node.

claims.claim: No automation for creating this storage billing policy and associating its Azure billing details is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 pay-as-you-go billing policy create Azure subscription resource group API PowerShell Microsoft Graph; SharePoint module New-SPOBillingPolicy; Graph billingPolicy beta. Read billing-node setup and New-SPOAppBillingPolicy; app/Backup policies are not this meter.

claims.claim: A subscription or resource group associated with a billing policy cannot be edited.
claims.quote: You can't edit a subscription or resource group associated with a billing policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Billing policies > policy > Budget > Settings opens budget configuration.
claims.quote: On the Billing policies tab, select a billing policy. In the billing policy side panel, select the Budget tab. To configure your budget and alert preferences, select Settings. Select the Set a budget for this policy checkbox.
claims.fix: Extend controls[2].ui.path to "Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Billing policies > policy > Budget > Settings > Set a budget for this policy". The cited billing-node article documents this checkbox and the budget and alert fields that follow.

claims.claim: No automation to configure this Microsoft 365 storage billing policy budget and alert thresholds is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 pay-as-you-go billing policy budget Settings API Microsoft Graph spending hard cap stop SharePoint Storage; Graph billingPolicy budget create update beta. Read billing-node setup and pay-as-you-go-budget search excerpts; no operation for this policy budget appeared.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; controls[3].api; Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Caps; Open questions
claims.claim: No hard spending cap or automatic budget stop for SharePoint Storage billing is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 pay-as-you-go billing policy budget Settings API Microsoft Graph spending hard cap stop SharePoint Storage. Read billing-node setup, add-storage-space and budget search excerpts; budgets do not stop billing, and no hard-cap operation or UI was documented.

claims.where: controls[4].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: SharePoint admin center > Active sites shows tenant storage used and total subscription storage.
claims.quote: In the navigation menu, select Active sites. The top of the Active sites page displays the amount of storage used across all sites, and the total storage for your subscription.

claims.claim: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/reports/getSharePointSiteUsageStorage(period='D7') retrieves the storage usage report.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/reports/getSharePointSiteUsageStorage(period='D7')

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Add more products > Office 365 > Office 365 Extra File Storage > Details reaches the add-on purchase page.
claims.quote: If you're using the Simplified view, select Billing, and then select Add more products. Under View by category, select Office 365. Find Office 365 Extra File Storage, and then select Details.
claims.fix: Restore the omitted heading: set controls[5].ui.path to "Billing > Add more products > View by category > Office 365 > Office 365 Extra File Storage > Details". Keep the existing Simplified view/MCA qualification.

claims.claim: No automation for purchasing the Office 365 Extra File Storage add-on is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Office 365 Extra File Storage purchase add-on API Microsoft Graph PowerShell commerce; SharePoint Online Management Shell Extra File Storage buy purchase storage quota cmdlet. Read add-storage-space and module search excerpts; quota-setting commands do not purchase capacity.

claims.claim: The quoted Extra File Storage purchase path is for Simplified view with an MCA account, and the MOSA route differs.
claims.quote: If you have an MCA billing account type: ... select Billing, and then select Add more products. If you have an MOSA billing account type: ... Select the subscription that you want to buy an add-on for.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; At rollout
claims.claim: The billing policy budget has a configurable reset period.
claims.quote: Select when to reset the budget spending: On the first day of the month; On the first day of the quarter; On the first day of the year.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; At rollout
claims.claim: Email-enabled groups can receive billing policy budget alerts.
claims.quote: Under Send email alerts, search for and select the names of email-enabled groups that you want to receive budget alerts.

claims.claim: Alert thresholds can be configured when creating the billing policy budget.
claims.quote: Under the Send alerts when usage reaches this percentage of budget section, the default value is 100%. To add other percentages, select Add more, and then enter the percentage at which you want an alert sent.

claims.claim: The billing policy Budget tab displays spending for its linked services.
claims.quote: On the Billing policies tab, select a billing policy. In the billing policy side panel, select the Budget tab. The Spending option displays data for the current month and includes a chart that displays data for the last six months.
